name: Caddy
works_with: A single executable with no external dependencies, downloaded from GitHub Releases. Building from source needs Go 1.26.0 or newer
short: A web server and reverse proxy that turns on HTTPS for your sites automatically.
what: Caddy is an extensible server platform, mostly used as an HTTPS server. It gets certificates from ZeroSSL and Let's Encrypt for public names, runs a local CA for internal names, and supports HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 by default. You configure it with a Caddyfile, its native JSON config, or its JSON API.
who: Developers and self-hosters who need to serve a site or put HTTPS in front of an app. Skip it if you already run a web server you are happy with and don't need automatic certificates.
needs: A machine to run it on. The release download is a single executable
Permission to bind to low ports (80, 443) if your config uses them
Go 1.26.0 or newer, only if you build from source

steps.title: Download Caddy
steps.text: Get the executable for your system from https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/releases and place it in your PATH. Other install methods are at https://caddyserver.com/docs/install.

steps.title: Or build from source
steps.text: These steps do not embed proper version information. Use xcaddy build for that, or to add plugins.
steps.code:
$ git clone "https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy.git"
$ cd caddy/cmd/caddy/
$ go build

steps.title: Allow low ports on Linux, if needed
steps.text: Only for a binary you built yourself that must bind to ports below 1024.

steps.title: Do the Getting Started guide
steps.text: The README recommends every user do it: https://caddyserver.com/docs/getting-started. Shorter quick-start tutorials are at https://caddyserver.com/docs/quick-starts.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Work through the Getting Started guide at https://caddyserver.com/docs/getting-started, or pick one of the quick-starts at https://caddyserver.com/docs/quick-starts.

watch: The README gives no first command. Its setup and config instructions are on caddyserver.com/docs, not in the repo README.
setcap gives the binary permission to bind to low ports. The README also shows a sudoers line to skip the password prompt for setcap and warns to do that only if you know what you are doing.
Automatic HTTPS requests certificates from public certificate authorities (ZeroSSL, Let's Encrypt) for public names.
The license is not stated in the README. Check the LICENSE file in the repo.
